We are enjoined to lay aside every hinderance, and to be prepared both for journey and for war. By nature we dislike exertion, and want agility. A rough road and many other obstacles retard our progress, and we are discouraged by the smallest annoyance. On these accounts, Paul holds out the gospel as the fittest means for undertaking and performing the expedition. Erasmus proposes a circumlocution, (<foreign xml:lang="la"><hi type="italic">ut sitis parati</hi></foreign>,) <hi type="italic">that ye may be</hi> <hi type="italic">prepared;</hi> but this does not appear to convey the true meaning.<div eID="gen125510" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.15" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125509" osisID="Eph.6.15" type="section"/>
entries.e428001c8454f0dbf4dd270672f25a3c744e1061: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.16" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.16" sID="gen125511" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125512" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16.</hi> <hi type="italic">Taking the shield of faith.</hi> Though <hi type="italic">faith</hi> and <hi type="italic">the</hi> <hi type="italic">word of God</hi> are one, yet Paul assigns to them two distinct offices. I call them one, because the word is the object of faith, and cannot be applied to our use but by faith; as faith again is nothing, and can do nothing, without the word. But Paul, neglecting so subtle a distinction, allowed himself to expatiate at large on the military armor. In the first Epistle to the Thessalonians he gives both to faith and to love the name of a <hi type="italic">breastplate,</hi> — “putting on the breastplate of faith and love,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:1Thess.5.8">1 Thessalonians 5:8</reference>.) All that was intended, therefore, was obviously this, — “He who possesses the excellencies of character which are here described is protected on every hand.”<div eID="gen125512" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125513" type="x-p"/>And yet it is not without reason that the most necessary instruments of warfare — a sword and a shield — are compared to faith, and to the word of God. In the spiritual combat, these two hold the highest rank. By faith we repel all the attacks of the devil, and by the word of God the enemy himself is slain. If the word of God shall have its efficacy upon us through faith, we shall be more than sufficiently armed both for opposing the enemy and for putting him to flight. And what shall we say of those who take from a Christian people the word of God? Do they not rob them of the necessary armor, and leave them to perish without a struggle? There is no man of any rank who is not bound to be a soldier of Christ. But if we enter the field unarmed, if we want our sword, how shall we sustain that character?<div eID="gen125513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125514" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">Wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the darts.</hi> But <hi type="italic">quench</hi> appears not to be the proper word. Why did he not use, instead of it, <hi type="italic">ward off</hi> or <hi type="italic">shake off,</hi> or some such word? <hi type="italic">Quench</hi> is far more expressive; for it is adapted to the epithet applied to <hi type="italic">darts</hi> <hi type="italic">The darts</hi> of Satan are not only sharp and penetrating, but — what makes them more destructive — they are <hi type="italic">fiery</hi> Faith will be found capable, not only of blunting their edge, but of <hi type="italic">quenching</hi> their heat.<div eID="gen125514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125515" type="x-p"/>“This,” says John, “is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.” (<reference osisRef="Bible:1John.5.4">1 John 5:4</reference>.)<div eID="gen125515" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.16" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125511" osisID="Eph.6.16" type="section"/>
entries.2b1051df8ace55835d38115e9609e720934cad02: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.17" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.17" sID="gen125516" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125517" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17.</hi> <hi type="italic">And take the helmet of salvation.</hi> In a passage already quoted, (<reference osisRef="Bible:1Thess.5.8">1 Thessalonians 5:8</reference>,) “the <hi type="italic">hope</hi> of salvation” is said to be a <hi type="italic">helmet,</hi> which I consider to be in the same sense as this passage. The head is protected by the best <hi type="italic">helmet,</hi> when, elevated by <hi type="italic">hope,</hi> we look up towards heaven to that <hi type="italic">salvation</hi> which is promised. It is only therefore by becoming the object of <hi type="italic">hope</hi> that <hi type="italic">salvation</hi> is a <hi type="italic">helmet.</hi><div eID="gen125517" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.17" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125516" osisID="Eph.6.17" type="section"/>
entries.5db14fd6b3ab8a7a5c538cd4ff2ae1309c80c2eb: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.18" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.18" sID="gen125518" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125519" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18.</hi> <hi type="italic">Praying always with all prayer.</hi> Having instructed the Ephesians to put on their armor, he now enjoins them to fight by prayer. This is the true method. To call upon God is the chief exercise of faith and hope; and it is in this way that we obtain from God every blessing. <hi type="italic">Prayer</hi> and <hi type="italic">supplication</hi> are not greatly different from each other, except that <hi type="italic">supplication</hi> is only one branch of <hi type="italic">prayer</hi><div eID="gen125519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125520" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">With all perseverance.</hi> We are exhorted to persevere in prayer. Every tendency to weariness must be counteracted by a cheerful performance of the duty. With unabated ardor we must continue our prayers, though we do not immediately obtain what we desire. If, instead of <hi type="italic">with all perseverance,</hi> some would render it, <hi type="italic">with all</hi> Earnestness, I would have no objection to the change.<div eID="gen125520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125521" type="x-p"/>But what is the meaning of <hi type="italic">always?</hi> Having already spoken of continued application, does he twice repeat the same thing? I think not. When everything flows on prosperously, — when we are easy and cheerful, we seldom feel any strong excitement to prayer, — or rather, we never flee to God, but when we are driven by some kind of distress. Paul therefore desires us to allow no opportunity to pass, — on no occasion to neglect prayer; so that <hi type="italic">praying always</hi> is the same thing with praying both in prosperity and in adversity.<div eID="gen125521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125522" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">For all saints.</hi> There is not a moment of our life at which the duty of prayer may not be urged by our own wants. But unremitting prayer may likewise be enforced by the consideration, that the necessities of our brethren ought to move our sympathy. And when is it that some members of the church are not suffering distress, and needing our assistance? If, at any time, we are colder or more indifferent about prayer than we ought to be, because we do not feel the pressure of immediate necessity, — let us instantly reflect how many of our brethren are worn out by varied and heavy afflictions, — are weighed down by sore perplexity, or are reduced to the lowest distress. If reflections like these do not rouse us from our lethargy, we must have hearts of stone. But are we to pray for believers only? Though the apostle states the claims of the godly, he does not exclude others. And yet in prayer, as in all other kind offices, our first care unquestionably is due to the saints.<div eID="gen125522" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.18" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125518" osisID="Eph.6.18" type="section"/>
entries.79174ac5730cc6f9338c645b43a4e4c7df5e49dd: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.19" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.19" sID="gen125523" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125524" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19.</hi> <hi type="italic">And for me.</hi> For himself, in a particular manner, he enjoins the Ephesians to pray. Hence we infer that there is no man so richly endowed with gifts as not to need this kind of assistance from his brethren, so long as he remains in this world. Who will ever be better entitled to plead exemption from this necessity than Paul? Yet he entreats the prayers of his brethren, and not hypocritically, but from an earnest desire of their aid. And what does he wish that they should ask for him?<hi type="italic"> That utterance may be given to me.</hi> What then? Was he habitually dumb, or did fear restrain him from making an open profession of the gospel? By no means; but there was reason to fear lest his splendid commencement should not be sustained by his future progress. Besides, his zeal for proclaiming the gospel was so ardent that he was never satisfied with his exertions. And indeed, if we consider the weight and importance of the subject, we shall all acknowledge that we are very far from being able to handle it in a proper manner. Accordingly he adds,<div eID="gen125524" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.19" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125523" osisID="Eph.6.19" type="section"/>
entries.129dca99e1b5776495bf612a4c4a6998c173471f:
20. As I ought to speak; meaning, that to proclaim the truth of the gospel as it ought to be proclaimed, is a high and rare attainment. Every word here deserves to be carefully weighed. Twice he uses the expression boldly, — “that I may open my mouth boldly,” “that therein I may speak boldly.” Fear hinders us from preaching Christ openly and fearlessly, while the absence of all restraint and disguise in confessing Christ is demanded from his ministers. Paul does not ask for himself the powers of an acute debater, or, I should rather say, of a dexterous sophist, that he might shield himself from his enemies by false pretences. It is, that I may open my mouth, to make a clear and strong confession; for when the mouth is half shut, the sounds which it utters are doubtful and confused. To open the mouth, therefore, is to speak with perfect freedom, without the smallest dread.
But does not Paul discover unbelief, when he entertains doubts as to his own stedfastness, and implores the intercession of others? No. He does not, like unbelievers, seek a remedy which is contrary to the will of God, or inconsistent with his word. The only aids on which he relies are those which he knows to be sanctioned by the Divine promise and approbation. It is the command of God, that believers shall pray for one another. How consoling then must it be to each of them to learn that the care of his salvation is enjoined on all the rest, and to be informed by God himself that the prayers of others on his behalf are not poured out in vain! Would it be lawful to refuse what the Lord himself has offered? Each believer, no doubt, ought to have been satisfied with the Divine assurance, that as often as he prayed he would be heard. But if, in addition to all the other manifestations of his kindness, God were pleased to declare that he will listen to the prayers of others in our behalf, would it be proper that this bounty should be slighted, or rather, ought we not to embrace it with open arms?
Let us therefore remember that Paul, when he resorted to the intercessions of his brethren, was influenced by no distrust or hesitation. His eagerness to obtain them arose from his resolution that no privilege which the Lord had given him should be overlooked. How absurdly then do Papists conclude from Paul’s example, that we ought to pray to the dead! Paul was writing to the Ephesians, to whom he had it in his power to communicate his sentintents. But what intercourse have we with the dead? As well might they argue that we ought to invite angels to our feasts and entertainments, because among men friendship is promoted by such kind offices.
Ephesians 6:21-24
21. But that ye also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things:
21. Ut autem sciatis vos etiam quae circa me aguntur, quid faciam, omnia vobis patefaciet Tychicus, dilectus frater et fidelis minister in Domino;
22. Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts.
22. Quem misi ad vos in eum finem, ut statum meum cognosceretis, et consolaretur corda vestra.
23. Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ
23. Pax fratribus, et dilectio cum fide a Deo Patre et Domino Iesu Christo.
24. Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.
24. Gratia cum omnibus, qui diligunt Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum in sinceritate. Amen.
entries.8cbc3eee6778c58c72e85fdd1304f33cdfd62ca8: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.21" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.21" sID="gen125540" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125541" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21.</hi> <hi type="italic">But that, ye also may know.</hi> Uncertain or false reports frequently produce uneasiness, chiefly, no doubt, in weak minds, but sometimes also in thoughtful and steady persons. To prevent this danger, Paul sends Tychicus, from whom the Ephesians would receive full information. The holy solicitude which Paul felt about the interests of religion, or, to use his own language, “the care of all the churches,” (<reference osisRef="Bible:2Cor.11.28">2 Corinthians 11:28</reference>,) was thus strikingly evinced. When death stood constantly before his eyes, neither the dread of death, nor anxiety about himself, prevented him from making provision for the most distant churches. Another man would have said, “My own affairs require all the attention I can give. It would be more reasonable that all should run to my assistance, than that they should expect from me the smallest relief.” But Paul acts a different part, and sends in every direction to strengthen the churches which he had founded.<div eID="gen125541" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125542" type="x-p"/>Tychicus is commended, that his statements may be more fully believed. <hi type="italic">A faithful minister in the Lord.</hi> It is not easy to say, whether this refers to the public ministry of the church, or to the private attentions which Paul had received from Tychicus. This uncertainty arises from these two expressions being connected, <hi type="italic">a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord.</hi> The former refers to Paul, to whom the second may be supposed also to apply. I am more inclined, however, to understand it as denoting the public ministry; for I do not think it probable that Paul would have sent any man who did not hold such a rank in the church, as would secure the respectful attention of the Ephesians.<div eID="gen125542" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.21" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125540" osisID="Eph.6.21" type="section"/>
entries.0f4f164dee9168d611edeec9449b22740a1c202c: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.23" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.23" sID="gen125543" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125544" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23.</hi> <hi type="italic">Peace be to the brethren.</hi> I consider the word <hi type="italic">peace,</hi> as in the salutations of the Epistles, to mean <hi type="italic">prosperity.</hi> Yet if the reader shall prefer to view it as signifying <hi type="italic">harmony,</hi> because, immediately afterwards, Paul mentions <hi type="italic">love,</hi> I do not object to that interpretation, or rather, it agrees better with the context. He wishes the Ephesians to be peaceable and quiet among themselves; and this, he presently adds, may be obtained by brotherly <hi type="italic">love</hi> and by agreement in <hi type="italic">faith</hi> From this prayer we learn that <hi type="italic">faith</hi> and <hi type="italic">love,</hi> as well as <hi type="italic">peace</hi> itself, are gifts of God bestowed upon us through Christ, — that they come equally <hi type="italic">from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.</hi><div eID="gen125544" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.23" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125543" osisID="Eph.6.23" type="section"/>
entries.b84a25bba6ceded14698efe6845a7d4782ba6794: <div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.24" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Eph.6.24" sID="gen125545" type="section"/> <div sID="gen125546" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24.</hi> <hi type="italic">Grace be with all.</hi> The meaning is, “May God continue to bestow his favor on all who love Jesus Christ with a pure conscience!” The Greek word, which I follow Erasmus in translating <hi type="italic">sincerity,</hi> (ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ,) signifies literally <hi type="italic">uncorruptedness,</hi> which deserves attention on account of the beauty of the metaphor. Paul intended to state indirectly, that, when the heart of man is free from all hypocrisy, it will be free from all corruption. This prayer conveys to us the instruction, that the only way of enjoying the light of the Divine countenance is to love <hi type="italic">sincerely</hi> God’s own Son, in whom his love toward us has been declared and confirmed. But let there be no hypocrisy; for most men, while they are not unwilling to make some professions of religion, entertain exceedingly low notions of Christ, and worship him with pretended homage. I wish there were not so many instances in the present day to prove that Paul’s admonition, to <hi type="italic">love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity</hi> is as necessary as ever.<div eID="gen125546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125547" type="x-p"/>END OF THE COMMENTARIES ON THE EPISTLE TO THE EPHESIANS.<div eID="gen125547" type="x-p"/><div annotateRef="Bible:Eph.6.24" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen125545" osisID="Eph.6.24" type="section"/><div eID="gen125529"/><div eID="gen125403"/><div eID="gen124404"/> <div sID="gen125548"/> <div sID="gen125549" type="x-p"/>A TRANSLATION OF<div eID="gen125549" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125550" type="x-p"/>CALVIN’S VERSION OF THE<div eID="gen125550" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125551" type="x-p"/>EPISTLE OF PAUL TO THE GALATIANS.<div eID="gen125551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125552"/> <div sID="gen125553" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 1<div eID="gen125553" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125554" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Paul, an apostle, not from men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,<div eID="gen125554" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125555" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>And all the brethren who are with met to the churches of Galatia;<div eID="gen125555" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125556" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Grace (be) to you, and peace from God the Father, and (from) our Lord Jesus Christ,<div eID="gen125556" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125557" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from the present wicked age, according to the will of God and our Father,<div eID="gen125557" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125558" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>To whom (be) glory for ever and ever. sID="gen125560" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Par grace, ou, en la grace de Christ</foreign>.” “By grace, or, in the grace of Christ.”<div eID="gen125560" type="x-p"/> </note> to another Christ.<div eID="gen125561" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125562" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>But although we, or an angel from heaven preach the gospel to you otherwise than what we have preached type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And James, and Cephas, and John, (who seethed to be pillars,) having known the grace given to me, gave to me and to Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, that we That I might live to God,<div eID="gen125607" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125608" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>I am crucified with Christ. <note n="181"> <div sID="gen125609" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Car par la Loy je suis mort a la Loy, et suis crucifie avec Christ, afin que je vive a Dieu</foreign>.” “For by the Law I am dead to the Law, and am crucified with Christ, that I may live to God.”<div eID="gen125609" type="x-p"/> </note> Now it is no longer I that live, but Christ liveth in me; and that I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.<div eID="gen125608" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125610" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>I do not set aside the grace of God; for, if righteousness is by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.<div eID="gen125610" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen125586"/> <div sID="gen125611"/> <div sID="gen125612" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 3<div eID="gen125612" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125613" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>O foolish Galatians, who hath enchanted you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes hath been clearly exhibited Jesus, Christ crucified among you?<div eID="gen125613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125614" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>This only I wish to learn from you; Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the preaching of faith?<div eID="gen125614" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125615" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Are ye so foolish, that, having begun by the Spirit, ye are now completed by the flesh?<div eID="gen125615" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125616" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be indeed in vain.<div eID="gen125616" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125617" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, (doth he it) by the works of the law, or by the preaching of faith?<div eID="gen125617" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125618" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Even as Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Gen.15.6">Genesis 15:6</reference> <reference osisRef="Bible:Rom.4.3">Romans 4:3</reference> <reference osisRef="Bible:Jas.2.23">James 2:23</reference>.)<div eID="gen125618" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125619" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Know ye therefore that they who are of faith are the children of Abraham.<div eID="gen125619" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125620" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>And the scripture, because it foresaw <note n="182"> <div sID="gen125621" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Prevoyant</foreign>.” “Foreseeing.”<div eID="gen125621" type="x-p"/> </note> that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, formerly preached the gospel to Abraham: In thee shall all nations be blessed.<div eID="gen125620" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125622" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And so they who are of faith are blessed with believing Abraham.<div eID="gen125622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125623" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>For all that are of the works of the law are under a curse; for it is written, (<reference osisRef="Bible:Deut.22.6">Deuteronomy 22:6</reference>,) Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.<div eID="gen125623" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125624" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Now that by the law no man is instilled before God is evident, for the just by faith shall live. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Hab.2.4">Habakkuk 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Bible:Rom.1.17">Romans 1:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Bible:Heb.10.38">Hebrews 10:38</reference>.)<div eID="gen125624" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125625" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>And the law is not of faith; but the man who shall do these things shall live in them. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Lev.18.5">Leviticus 18:5</reference>.)<div eID="gen125625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125626" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, having been made a curse for us; (for it is written, (<reference osisRef="Bible:Deut.21.23">Deuteronomy 21:23</reference>,) Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree;)<div eID="gen125626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125627" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>That the blessing of Abraham may come upon the Gentiles by Christ Jesus; that we may receive the promise of the Spirit by faith.<div eID="gen125627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125628" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>Brethren, (I speak after the manner of men,) though it be but a man’s covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man setteth aside or addeth any thing.<div eID="gen125628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125629" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Now to Abraham were the promises spoken, and to his seed. type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125631" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>For, if the inheritance (is) by the law, (it is) no longer by promise; but God gave it to Abraham by promise.<div eID="gen125631" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125632" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>To what then serveth the law? <note n="183"> <div sID="gen125633" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">A quoy donc sert la a mediator.<div eID="gen125632" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125634" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>Now the mediator is not of one; but God is one.<div eID="gen125634" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125635" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>(Is) the law then against the promises of God? <note n="184"> <div sID="gen125636" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Ou, a elle este adjoustee certainly righteousness would have been by the law.<div eID="gen125635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125638" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>But the scripture hath shut up all things under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.<div eID="gen125638" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125639" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Now before faith came, we were guarded under the law, shut up to the faith which was to be revealed.<div eID="gen125639" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125640" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.<div eID="gen125640" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125641" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>But faith being come, <note n="186"> <div sID="gen125642" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">La foy estant venue</foreign>.”<div eID="gen125642" type="x-p"/> </note> we are no longer under a schoolmaster.<div eID="gen125641" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125643" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.<div eID="gen125643" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125644" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27 </hi>For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.<div eID="gen125644" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125645" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28 </hi>There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female; for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.<div eID="gen125645" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125646" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29 </hi>And if ye are Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.<div eID="gen125646" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen125611"/> <div sID="gen125647"/> <div sID="gen125648" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 4<div eID="gen125648" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125649" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Now I say: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a slave, <note n="187"> <div sID="gen125650" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Il n’est different en rien du serf</foreign>.” “He is not different in any respect from the slave.”<div eID="gen125650" type="x-p"/> </note> though he is lord of all;<div eID="gen125649" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125651" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>But is under tutors and guardians, till the time appointed by the father.<div eID="gen125651" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125652" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>So also we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world.<div eID="gen125652" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125653" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>But when the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, subjected under the law;<div eID="gen125653" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125654" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>That he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive adoption. <note n="188"> <div sID="gen125655" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">A celle fin que receussions l’adoption des enfans</foreign>.” “To this end, that we might receive the adoption of sons.”<div eID="gen125655" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen125654" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125656" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.<div eID="gen125656" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125657" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Wherefore thou art no longer a slave <note n="189"> <div sID="gen125658" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Maintenant tu n’es plus serf</foreign>.”<div eID="gen125658" type="x-p"/> </note> but a son; and if a son, likewise an heir of God by Christ.<div eID="gen125657" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125659" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>But at the time when ye knew not God, ye served those who by nature are not gods.<div eID="gen125659" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125660" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>But now, after that ye have known God, or rather have been known by God, why do ye turn again to the weak and beggarly elements, which you again desire to serve, anew? <note n="190"> <div sID="gen125661" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Ausquels vous voulez derechef servir comme auparavant</foreign>.” “Which you desire again to serve as formerly.”<div eID="gen125661" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen125660" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125662" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.<div eID="gen125662" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125663" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>I am afraid of you, lest perhaps I have labored among you in vain.<div eID="gen125663" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125664" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Be ye as I; for I also am as you. Brethren, I beseech you; ye have done me no injury.<div eID="gen125664" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125665" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Now ye knew that, through infirmity of the flesh, I formerly preached the gospel to you;<div eID="gen125665" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125666" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And the trial of me, which was in my flesh, ye despised not, nor rejected; <note n="191"> <div sID="gen125667" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Et n’avez point mesprise ne rejette l’espreuve de moy, telle qu’elle estoit en ma chair</foreign>.” “And ye despised not, nor rejected, the trial of me, such as it was in my flesh.”<div eID="gen125667" type="x-p"/> </note> but ye received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.<div eID="gen125666" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125668" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>Where is then your blessedness? for I bear you witness, that, if it had been possible, ye would even have plucked out your own eyes, and would have given them to me.<div eID="gen125668" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125669" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Am I therefore become your enemy by speaking the truth?<div eID="gen125669" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125670" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>They are jealous of you, not well; <note n="192"> <div sID="gen125671" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Non point pour bien</foreign>.” “Not for good.”<div eID="gen125671" type="x-p"/> </note> yea, they wish to exclude you, that ye may be jealous of them.<div eID="gen125670" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125672" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>But it is good to be the object of jealousy always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.<div eID="gen125672" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125673" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>My little children, for whom I again travail in birth; till Christ be formed in you,<div eID="gen125673" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125674" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>I would wish now to be present with you, and to change my voice; for I am distressed about you.<div eID="gen125674" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125675" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>Tell me, ye who wish to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?<div eID="gen125675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125676" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>For it is written, that Abraham had two sons; one by the bond-maid, the other by the free-woman.<div eID="gen125676" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125677" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>But he who (was) of the bond-maid was born according to the flesh; but he who, (was) of the free-woman, by promise.<div eID="gen125677" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125678" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>Which things are allegorical <note n="193"> <div sID="gen125679" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Lesquelles choses sent dites par allegorie</foreign>.” “Which things are spoken by allegory.”<div eID="gen125679" type="x-p"/> </note> for there are two covenants; one indeed from mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, that is Agar.<div eID="gen125678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125680" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>For Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and, on the other hand, corresponds to that which is now Jerusalem; for she is in bondage with her children.<div eID="gen125680" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125681" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>But Jerusalem, which is above, is free, which is the mother of us all.<div eID="gen125681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125682" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27 </hi>For it is written: Rejoice, O barren, who bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not; for more are the children of the forsaken than of her who hath a husband. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Isa.54.1">Isaiah 54:1</reference>.)<div eID="gen125682" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125683" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28 </hi>Now we, brethren, like Isaac, are children of the promise. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Rom.9.7">Romans 9:7</reference>.)<div eID="gen125683" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125684" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29 </hi>But as, at that time, he who was born according to the flesh, persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit; so also is it now.<div eID="gen125684" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125685" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30 </hi>But what saith the scripture? Cast out the bond-maid, and her son; for the son of the bond-maid shall not obtain the inheritance with the so, of the free-woman.<div eID="gen125685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125686" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31 </hi>Wherefore, brethren, we are not children of the bond-woman, but of the free.<div eID="gen125686" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen125647"/> <div sID="gen125687"/> <div sID="gen125688" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 5<div eID="gen125688" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125689" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Stand fast, therefore, in the liberty with which Christ hath made us free; and be not again entangled by the yoke of bondage.<div eID="gen125689" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125690" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Behold, I Paul protest to you, that, if ye be circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.<div eID="gen125690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125691" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>For I testify again to every man who is circumcised that he is a debtor to do the whole law.<div eID="gen125691" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125692" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Whosoever of you are justified by the law, ye have separated yourselves from Christ; ye are fallen from grace.<div eID="gen125692" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125693" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>For we, through the Spirit, by faith, wait for the hope of righteousness.<div eID="gen125693" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125694" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith working by love.<div eID="gen125694" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125695" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Ye were running well. Who hindered you, that ye should not obey the truth?<div eID="gen125695" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125696" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>This persuasion is not from him who called you.<div eID="gen125696" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125697" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.<div eID="gen125697" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125698" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>I am persuaded concerning you in the Lord, that ye will think nothing else; <note n="194"> <div sID="gen125699" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Que vous n’aurez autre sentiment</foreign>.” “That ye will have no other opinion.”<div eID="gen125699" type="x-p"/> </note> but he that troubleth you shall bear the condemnation, whoever he be.<div eID="gen125698" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125700" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>And I, <note n="195"> <div sID="gen125701" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Et quant a moy</foreign>.” “And as to myself.”<div eID="gen125701" type="x-p"/> </note> brethren, if I still preach circumcision, why do I still suffer persecution? The offense of the cross is abolished.<div eID="gen125700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Would that they were even cut off who trouble you!<div eID="gen125702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125703" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>For ye, brethren, have been called to liberty; only make not the liberty an occasion to the flesh, <note n="196"> <div sID="gen125704" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Seulement (gardez) que la liberte ne soit occasion a la chair</foreign>.” “Only beware lest the liberty be an occasion to the flesh.”<div eID="gen125704" type="x-p"/> </note> but by love serve one another.<div eID="gen125703" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125705" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, namely, this: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.<div eID="gen125705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125706" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>But if ye bite and devour one another, see that ye be not consumed by one another.<div eID="gen125706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125707" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Now I say: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh.<div eID="gen125707" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125708" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit; and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, so that ye cannot do those things which ye would wish.<div eID="gen125708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125709" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>But if ye are led by the Spirit, ye are not under the law.<div eID="gen125709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125710" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,<div eID="gen125710" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125711" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>Idolatry, witchcraft, enmities, strife, emulations, wrath, quarrellings, seditions, heresies,<div eID="gen125711" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125712" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like; of which I foretell to you, as I also have foretold, that they who do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.<div eID="gen125712" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125713" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, long-suffering, <note n="197"> <div sID="gen125714" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Patience, ou esprit patient</foreign>.” “Patience, or a patient mind.”<div eID="gen125714" type="x-p"/> </note> gentleness, kindness, fidelity,<div eID="gen125713" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125715" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Meekness, temperance; against such there is no law.<div eID="gen125715" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125716" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>And they who are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.<div eID="gen125716" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125717" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.<div eID="gen125717" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125718" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>Let us not be desirous of vain-glory, provoking one another, envying one another.<div eID="gen125718" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen125687"/> <div sID="gen125719"/> <div sID="gen125720" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 6<div eID="gen125720" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125721" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Brethren, although a man be overtaken in any fault, ye, who are spiritual, restore such a man in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.<div eID="gen125721" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125722" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Bear ye one another’s burdens, and thus fulfill the law of Christ.<div eID="gen125722" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125723" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>For if any one thinketh himself to be something, though he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.<div eID="gen125723" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125724" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>But let every one prove his own work; and then shall he have glory in himself alone, and not in another. <note n="198"> <div sID="gen125725" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Et alors il aura dequoy se glorifier</foreign>.” “And then will ye have ground of boasting.”<div eID="gen125725" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen125724" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125726" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>For every one shall bear his own burden.<div eID="gen125726" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125727" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Let him who is taught in the word communicate to the teacher in all good things.<div eID="gen125727" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125728" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Do not mistake: God is not mocked; for what a man shall have sowed, that will he also reap.<div eID="gen125728" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125729" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>For he who soweth to his flesh, shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he who soweth to the Spirit, shall of the Spirit reap everlasting life.<div eID="gen125729" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125730" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And let us not weary in doing good; for if we do not faint, we shall reap in due time. <note n="199"> <div sID="gen125731" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Nous moissonnerons en la saison</foreign>.” “We shall reap in the season.”<div eID="gen125731" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen125730" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125732" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Therefore, while we have opportunity, let us do good to all, but especially to them who are of the household of faith.<div eID="gen125732" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125733" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Ye see what a letter <note n="200"> <div sID="gen125734" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Vous voyez (ou, voyez) quelles grandes lettres</foreign>.” “Ye see, (or, See ye) how long a letter.”<div eID="gen125734" type="x-p"/> </note> I have written with my own hand.<div eID="gen125733" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125735" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>As many as wish to please outwardly in the flesh, <note n="201"> <div sID="gen125736" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Tous ceux qui veuleut selon la face plaire en la chair, ou, Tous ceux qui cherchent belle apparence en la chair</foreign>.” “All those who wish according to the face to please in the flesh, or, All those who seek a fine show in the flesh.”<div eID="gen125736" type="x-p"/> </note> they constrain you to be circumcised; only that they may not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.<div eID="gen125735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125737" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>For neither they who hold by circumcision do themselves keep the law; but they wish you to be circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.<div eID="gen125737" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125738" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>But far be it from me to glory, unless in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.<div eID="gen125738" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125739" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth anything nor uncircumcision; but a new creature.<div eID="gen125739" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125740" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>And as many as walk by this rule, peace (be) on them, and mercy, and on the Israel of God.<div eID="gen125740" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125741" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Henceforth let no man give me annoyance; for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.<div eID="gen125741" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125742" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ (be) with your spirit. sID="gen125747" type="x-p"/>OF THE<div eID="gen125747" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125748" type="x-p"/>EPISTLE OF PAUL TO THE EPHESIANS.<div eID="gen125748" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125749"/> <div sID="gen125750" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 1<div eID="gen125750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125751" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus, and to the believers in Christ Jesus;<div eID="gen125751" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125752" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Grace (be) to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.<div eID="gen125752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125753" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Blessed <note n="202"> <div sID="gen125754" type="x-p"/> “<foreign blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heavenly <note n="203"> <div sID="gen125755" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Es (choses) celestes, ou, Es lieux celestes</foreign>.” “In heavenly things, or, In heavenly places.”‘‘<div eID="gen125755" type="x-p"/> </note> (places) in Christ;<div eID="gen125753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125756" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>As he hath </hi>Who hath predestinated us in adoption in himself through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will,<div eID="gen125757" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125758" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>To the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he hath made us accepted in the Beloved.<div eID="gen125758" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125759" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins,<div eID="gen125759" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125760" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>According to the riches of his his will, according to his good pleasure, which he had purposed in himself;<div eID="gen125761" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125762" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>In order to the dispensation of of the times.”<div eID="gen125763" type="x-p"/> </note> that he might gather together all things in Christ, both those things which are in heaven, and those things which are on the earth, in him;<div                <ns0:p n="6">6. Not with eye-service <ns0:hi>v</ns0:hi> as men-pleasers <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Such as make it their onely business to please their Masters right or wrong, and ingratiate themselves with them though by offending God.</ns0:note>, but as the servants of Christ <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">As becomes the Servants of Christ, or as those that are the Servants of Christ and seek to please him.</ns0:note>, doing the will of God <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Perfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ming obedience to your Masters not barely as their will, but God's will who requires it, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5.</ns0:note> from the heart.<ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Not merely having respect to your Masters presence, and looking upon you in your work.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7. With good will <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Not grudgingly or as of constraint, but freely, and cheerfully.</ns0:note> doing service as to the Lord, and not to men <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Not onely regarding Men your Masters, but Christ your great Master. That which is done for the worst Masters, and in the hardest things is Service done to Christ; when out of love to him Servants bear their Masters folly, or cruelty.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 2.6. 2 Cor. 5.10.</ns0:note> Knowing that whatsoever good thing <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> as the Servant of Christ and as unto the Lord.</ns0:note> any man doth, the same <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The reward of the same; by a Metonymie.</ns0:note> shall he receive of the Lord whether <ns0:hi>he be</ns0:hi> bond or free <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Christ re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gards not those differences of Men at the present, nor will in the day of Judgment, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.22. and 12, 13. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.28. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 3.11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9. And ye masters do the same things <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Not the same in special which belong onely to Servants, but in general which concern you no less than them, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> doe your duty to them with good will, with an Eye to God, and Christ, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> or rather, doe your duty mutually to them accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to your condition, and calling, <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 4.1.</ns0:note> to them, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>mode<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rating.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> forbearing <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Or rather (as in the margin) <ns0:hi>moderating,</ns0:hi> or remitting, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> do not carry your selves angrily to them (which appears in vehe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, and frequent threatnings) when ye may otherwise maintain your Authority over them.</ns0:note> threatning, knowing, that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Some reade,</ns0:hi> both your & their master.</ns0:note> your master also is in heaven <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And therefore too strong for you, though ye may be too hard for your Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 2.11.</ns0:note> neither is there respect of persons with him <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">He is just as well as powerfull, and will neither spare ye because you are Masters, nor punish them because they are Servants, see <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 10.34. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.6. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 3.25.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:491" />10<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Finally, my brethren, be strong <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>strengthen your selves,</ns0:hi> i. e. be courageous, and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stant in the practice of your duty against the Devil, and all his assaults.</ns0:note> in the Lord <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Not in your selves, but in the Lord Jesus Christ in whom your strength lies, and from whom by Faith ye may obtain it, see <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.13. and 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.1.</ns0:note> and in the power of his might <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>migh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty power,</ns0:hi> see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.19. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> though your own strength be but weakness, yet Christ's power is mighty, and he can com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municate enough to you.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 13.12. 2 Cor. 6.7.</ns0:note> Put on the whole armour <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Get your selves furnished with every Grace, that none be wanting in you, no part naked and exposed to your ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies.</ns0:note> of God <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Not carnal but spiritual, and given by God, see 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.3, 4. and 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.8.</ns0:note>, that ye may be able to stand <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Either to fight, or ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther to overcome. He that loses the Victory is said to fall; he that gains it, to stand, see <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 89.43.</ns0:note> against the wiles <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Devil useth Arts, and Strategems, as well as force and violence, and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore if any part of your spiritual armour be wanting he will Assault you where he finds you weakest.</ns0:note> of the devil.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12. For we wrestle not <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Not onely or not principally.</ns0:note> against <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>bloud, and flesh.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> flesh and bloud <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Men, consisting of flesh and bloud, <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 16.17. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 1.16.</ns0:note>, but against principalities, against powers <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Devils, <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 2.15. see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.21.</ns0:note>, against the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Joh. 12.31. Col. 1.13.</ns0:note> rulers of the darkness of this world <ns0:hi>v,</ns0:hi> against <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>wicked spirits.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> spiritual wickedness <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Either wicked Spirits, or Emphatically <ns0:hi>spiritual wickednesses</ns0:hi> for wickednesses of the highest kind, implying the intenseness of wickedness in those Angelical substances, which are so much the more wicked, by how much the more excellent in themselves their Natures are.</ns0:note> in <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>heavenly.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> high <ns0:hi>places</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>Heavenly,</ns0:hi> taking heaven for the whole <ns0:hi>expansum</ns0:hi> or spreading out of the Air between the Earth and the Stars, the Air being the place from whence the Devils assault us, as <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.2. Or rather <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>about</ns0:hi> heavenly places or things, in the same sense as the word rendred heavenly is taken four times before in this Epistle, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.3.20. & 2.6. & 3.10. being in none of them taken for the Air; and the then sense must be, that we wrestle about heavenly places, or things, not with Flesh and Bloud, but with Principalities, with Powers, <ns0:hi>&c. Obj.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Gr.</ns0:hi> preposition will not bear this construction. <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> Let <ns0:hi>Chrysostom</ns0:hi> and other <ns0:hi>Greeks</ns0:hi> answer for that. They under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood their Language best, and they give this interpretation.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Either that Rule in the dark Air where God permits them to be for the punishment of Men, see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.2. or rather, that Rule in the dark places of the Earth, the dark minds of Men, and have their rule over them by reason of the darkness that is in them, in which respect the Devil is called the God of this World, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.4. and the Prince of it, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 14.30. So that the dark World here seems to be op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed to Children of light, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.8.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13. Wherefore take unto you the whole ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Times of Temptation, and Satan's greatest rage, see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.16.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>having overcome all.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> having done all <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">All that belongs to good Souldiers of Jesus Christ, all that we can doe being little enough to secure our standing.</ns0:note> to stand <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">As Conquerours doe that keep the Field not being beaten down, nor giving way.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14. Stand <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Standing here (in a different sense from what it was ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken in before) seems to imply watchfulness, readyness for the Combate, and keeping our places, (both as to our gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral and particular callings) if Souldiers leave their Ranks they endanger themselves.</ns0:note> therefore <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 11.5. Luk. 12.35. 1 Pet. 1.13.</ns0:note> having yourloyns girt about <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Having exhorted to put on the whole armour of God, he descends to the particular parts of it both defensive and offensive. We need not be over curious in en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quiring into the reason of the Names here given to the seve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral parts of a Christian's armour, and the Analogy between them and Corporal Arms, the Apostle using these Terms promiscuously, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.8. and designing onely to shew that what bodily Arms are to Souldiers, that these spiritual Arms might be to Christians<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> yet some reason may be given of these Denominations. He begins with the furniture for the loyns, the seat of strength, and alludes to the belt or mili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>dle, which was both for ornament and strength, and so is <ns0:hi>truth.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> with truth <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Understood either of the truth of Doctrine, or rather (because that comes in afterward under the title of the Sword of the Spirit) of soundness, and Sincerity of heart, than which nothing doth more beautifie or adorn a Christian. He alludes to <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 59.17. see, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.12. and 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.5, 19.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">2 Cor. 6.7.</ns0:note> having on the breast-plate of righteousness <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Righteousness of Conversation, consisting both in a resolvedness for good, and repentance for evil done, which is as a Breast-plate (that piece or armour which covers the whole Breast, and Belly) to a Christian; that resolvedness a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst sin fencing him against Temptation, and the conscience of well doing against the accusations of Men and Devils. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.3, 4. and 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15. And your feet shod <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">In allusion to the Greaves or military shoes with which Souldiers covered their feet and legs. A Christian's way lies through rough places, through Briars and Thorns, and therefore he needs this piece of armour. He must be prepa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red to hold the Faith, and confess Christ in the most diffi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cult times.</ns0:note> with the preparati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of the gospel of peace <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">With that furniture which the Gospel affords him, which being a Gospel of peace, and bringing the glad tidings of Reconciliation to God by Christ, prepares Men best to undergo the troubles of the World. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 16.33.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16. Above all <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Chiefly, <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 3.14. this he sets, as the principal part of the Christian armour, against the greatest Temptations, fie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry darts, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 5.8, 9. and 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 5.4.</ns0:note> taking the shield of faith <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Faith as recei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving Christ and the benefits of Redemption is compared to a shield (under which Souldiers were wont to shelter them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves against their enemies darts) as being a sort of univer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sal defence covering the whole Man, and guarding even the other parts of our spiritual armour.</ns0:note> wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry darts <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">It seems to be an al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lusion to the poysoned darts, some barbarous Nations were wont to use which enflamed the bodies they hit. By them he means all those violent Temptations which enflame Mens lusts. These fiery darts of Temptations faith is said to quench when by the help of Grace obtained of Christ, it over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />comes them.</ns0:note> of the wicked <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Devil, <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 13.19.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17. And take the helmet of salvation <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Salvation for the hope of Salvation, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.8. This follows faith, and is of kin to it. Souldiers dare not fight without their helmet: despair, to which the Devil tempts us, makes us quit our combate; whereas hope of Salvation makes us lift up our heads in the midst of Temptations, and afflictions. This likewise alludes to <ns0:hi>Isa..</ns0:hi> 59.17.</ns0:note>, and the sword of the Spirit <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either the spiritual sword, the war being spiritual, and the enemy spiritual, or rather the sword which the spirit of God fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisheth us with, and makes effectual in our hands.</ns0:note> which is the word of God <ns0:hi>p.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Doctrine of God in the scripture, called a two edged sword, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.16. and 2.12. which enters into the Soul, and di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vides between the most inward affections, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4.12. and cuts the sinews of the strongest Temptations, <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 4.4.7.10. and Conquers the Devil while it rescues Sinners from un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der his power. This relates to <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 49.2.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18. Praying always <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In every opportunity, so often as our own, or others necessities call us to it, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.17.</ns0:note>, with all prayer and sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plication <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Prayer when op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed to supplication seems to signifie petitioning for good things, and supplication the deprecating of evil, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.1.</ns0:note> in the Spirit <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Either our own Spirit with which we pray, so as not to draw nigh to God with our Mouth onely, as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 29.13. Or rather the Holy Spirit of God by whose assistance we pray, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.26, 27. <ns0:hi>Iude</ns0:hi> 20.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark. 13.33.</ns0:note> and watching there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />unto <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To Prayer, in opposition to sloth and security. See <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 26.41. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 4.2. and 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.7.</ns0:note> with all perseverance <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Constancy and continuance in Prayer in every condition adverse as well as prosperous, though Prayer be not present<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly answered, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 18.1.</ns0:note>, and supplication for all saints <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Not onely for our selves, but for our Brethren in the world, none being in so good a con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition but they may need our Prayers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 4.29. Col. 4.3. 2 Thess. 3.1.</ns0:note> And for me, that utterance <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>Speech, viz.</ns0:hi> both the things I am to speak, and the faculty of speaking as becomes the matter I deliver.</ns0:note> may be gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly, <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either, freely and confidently; the same as before in other words, or, openly and plainly in opposition to speaking closely, and in secret, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 8.32. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 11.14. and so it may have respect to the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moving of his bonds which were the present impediment of his so speaking.</ns0:note> to make known the mystery of the gospel.<ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>unto</ns0:hi> the opening of my Mouth, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> full and free pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fession of the truth without shame or fear.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:491" />20 For which <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 5.20.</ns0:note> I am an ambassadour <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Act. 28.20. Chap. 3.1.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>in a <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> in bonds <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For which Gospel I still continue, though a prisoner, in the Ambassy committed to me by Christ.</ns0:note>, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>thereof.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> therein I may speak boldly <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This may imply not onely free speaking, but free acting in all things whereby the Gospel may be propagated.</ns0:note>, as I ought to speak.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Col. 4.7.</ns0:note> that ye also <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">As well as other Churches.</ns0:note> may know my affairs <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">How I am used by the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> in my bonds.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> how I do <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Or, rather <ns0:hi>what</ns0:hi> I do, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> how I behave my self, see <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 28.30, 31.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">2 Tim. 4.12. Tit. 3.12.</ns0:note> Tychicus a beloved brother, and faithfull minister <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Minister is here ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken in a large sense for any that labour in the Gospel, such as were not onely ordinary Pastours, but Evangelists, and Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles themselves.</ns0:note> in the Lord, shall make known to you all things.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">That ye might not faint at my Tribulation, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3.13. it might be a comfort to them to hear that <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was well u<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed (setting aside his bonds) and had liberty to preach to those that came to him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23. Peace <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> to the brethren, and love, with faith <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">He prays for their continuance and encrease in these graces which already were begun in them.</ns0:note> from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Grace <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> with all them <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This is more extensive than the former, he prays here for all true beleivers every· where.</ns0:note> that love our Lord Jesus Christ in <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>with in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />corruption.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> sincerity. Amen.<ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Or, as the margin, with <ns0:hi>incorruption, i. e.</ns0:hi> so as that nothing can draw them off from the love of Christ, and so it implies constancy as well as Sincerity.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Written from Rome unto the Ephesians by Tychicus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
